```
#include <Arduino.h>

const int analogReadPin = A1;

void setup() {
  // Initialize serial communication and wait up to 2.5 seconds for a connection
  Serial.begin(115200);
  for (auto startNow = millis() + 2500; !Serial && millis() < startNow; delay(500));
  
  // Set DAC resolution to 12-bit for maximum precision
  analogWriteResolution(12);

  // set analog read resolution to 14 bit
  analogReadResolution(14);
  
  Serial.println("Writing voltage from A0");
  Serial.println("Wire A0 pin and A1 pin together, to have A1 pin read in voltages from A0");
}

void loop() {
  // write
  float writeBit[51] = {}; // 51 steps from 0 V to 5 V, 0.1 V increments
  float writeVoltage[51] = {};

  // read
  float readVoltage[51] = {};
  
  for (int i = 0; i <= 50; i++) {
    writeVoltage[i] = (0.1 * i);
    writeBit[i] = (writeVoltage[i] * 4095) / 5.121; // mapping the voltage to a specific bit in the dac
    analogWrite(DAC, writeBit[i]);

    delay(10); // delay between writing and reading. time to settle

    int readBit = analogRead(analogReadPin);
    readVoltage[i] = readBit * (5.121 / 16383.0);

    // write values
    Serial.print("Applied Voltage: ");
    Serial.print(writeVoltage[i]);
    Serial.println(" VDC");
    
    // read values
    Serial.print("Sensed Voltage: ");
    Serial.print(readVoltage[i], 3);
    Serial.println(" VDC");
    
    delay(5000);  
  }

  Serial.println("- Cycle completed, repeating...");
  delay(1000);
}

// create function for writing and reading voltage

// create function for exporting data

```

_**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Here’s what `src/comm.m#L1` does, line by line. In short: it listens to COM3, picks voltage values out of the Arduino’s text output, and stores them in two MATLAB arrays. It doesn’t plot or save them.

- `port = "COM3";` Sets the serial port MATLAB will listen to.
- `arduino = serialport(port, 115200, "Timeout", 10);` Opens that port at 115200 

 does, line by line. In short: it listens to COM3, picks voltage values out of the Arduino’s text output, and stores them in two MATLAB arrays. It doesn’t plot or save them.

- `port = "COM3";` Sets the serial port MATLAB will listen to.
- `arduino = serialport(port, 115200, "Timeout", 10);` Opens that port at 115200 baud. The 10-second timeout limits how long MATLAB waits for a line before `readline` errors.
- `configureTerminator(arduino, "LF");` Tells MATLAB that each message ends with a line feed, matching the Arduino’s .

- `appliedVoltage = zeros(1, 51);` Creates a 51-element array for the Arduino’s applied-voltage values, initially filled with zeros.
- `sensedVoltage = zeros(1, 51);` Creates a second 51-element array for the measured values.
- `appliedCount = 0;` Tracks how many applied-voltage values have been received.
- `sensedCount = 0;` Tracks how many sensed-voltage values have been received.

- `while appliedCount < 51 || sensedCount < 51` Keeps listening until both arrays have 51 values. The `||` means “or,” so it keeps going if either array is still incomplete.
- `line = strtrim(readline(arduino));` Waits for one line from the Arduino, reads it, and removes whitespace at the ends. For example: `Applied Voltage: 1.2 VDC`.

- `appliedMatch = regexp(...)` Checks whether the line has the applied-voltage format. The pattern looks for `Applied Voltage:`, then captures a number, then requires `VDC`. It ignores other lines, like startup messages.
- `if ~isempty(appliedMatch) && appliedCount < 51` Proceeds only if the line contained a matching value and the array isn’t already full.
- `appliedCount = appliedCount + 1;` Advances to the next array position.
- `appliedVoltage(appliedCount) = str2double(appliedMatch{1});` Converts the captured number from text to a numeric value and stores it in the array.

- `sensedMatch = regexp(...)` Does the same format check for lines beginning with `Sensed Voltage:`.
- The following `if` block increments `sensedCount` and stores that numeric value in `sensedVoltage`.

- `end` Closes the loop once both counts reach 51.
- `clear arduino;` Releases the serial connection. The two arrays remain in MATLAB’s workspace.

Because the Arduino waits five seconds between readings, collecting a full 51-value cycle takes about four minutes and fifteen seconds. Afterward, you can inspect `appliedVoltage` and `sensedVoltage` in MATLAB.

```
port = "COM3"; % Select the Arduino's serial port.
arduino = serialport(port, 115200, "Timeout", 10); % Open the port at 115200 baud; wait at most 10 seconds when reading.
configureTerminator(arduino, "LF"); % Treat a line feed as the end of each incoming line.

appliedVoltage = zeros(1, 51); % Preallocate space for 51 applied-voltage values.
sensedVoltage = zeros(1, 51); % Preallocate space for 51 measured-voltage values.
```
```
sampleCount = 0; % Count how many complete voltage pairs have been received.

while sampleCount < 51 % Keep reading until 51 valid pairs have been received.
	line = strtrim(readline(arduino)); % Read one complete serial line and remove whitespace at its ends.
	values = str2double(split(line, ",")); % Split a comma-separated line and convert its values to numbers.

	if numel(values) == 2 && all(isfinite(values)) % Accept only lines containing exactly two valid numbers.
		sampleCount = sampleCount + 1; % Advance to the next sample position.
		appliedVoltage(sampleCount) = values(1); % Store the first CSV value as the applied voltage.
		sensedVoltage(sampleCount) = values(2); % Store the second CSV value as the sensed voltage.
	end % Ignore startup and cycle-status lines that are not numeric pairs.
end % Finish collecting after both arrays contain 51 values.

clear arduino; % Close the serial connection; keep the voltage arrays in the workspace.

figure; % Open a new plot window.
plot(appliedVoltage, sensedVoltage, "-o", "LineWidth", 1.5); % Plot sensed voltage against applied voltage.
grid on; % Show a grid to make voltage values easier to read.
xlabel("Applied Voltage (V)"); % Label the horizontal axis.
ylabel("Sensed Voltage (V)"); % Label the vertical axis.
title("Sensed Voltage vs. Applied Voltage"); % Describe the plotted relationship.
```
